results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) completes Rp 6.54 trillion shareholder loan from PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) to PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC)
results.body: The article reports that PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) facilitated a shareholder loan (SHL) of Rp 6.54 trillion between its subsidiaries PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) and PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC) on 17 September 2026. JSMR holds 65% of JTT and JTT holds 40% of JJC, and the loan is intended to bridge JJC’s refinancing and other operational needs with an interest rate within the market range. The transaction reduces JSMR’s cash and cash equivalents by roughly Rp 6.54 trillion and increases other receivables by the same amount, while its total liabilities were about Rp 100 trillion as of June 2026; the loan has no immediate impact on revenue or expenses, and JSMR’s first‑half 2026 toll revenue rose 6.8% to Rp 9.5 trillion, net profit about Rp 1.9 trillion and EBITDA grew about 8%. Panin Sekuritas analyst Elandry Pratama recommends a “buy on weakness” for JSMR with a target price of Rp 3,800–4,000 per share, noting the loan supports JJC’s liquidity while increasing intra‑group funding exposure.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) completes a IDR 6.54 trillion shareholder loan and is recommended as a buy
results.body: On 17 September 2026, PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) facilitated a IDR 6.54 trillion shareholder loan from its 65%-owned subsidiary PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) to JTT’s 40%-owned subsidiary PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC), reducing JSMR’s cash and cash equivalents by the same amount while leaving its revenue and expenses unchanged. Panin Sekuritas Pondok Indah analyst Elandry Pratama projects continued toll‑traffic growth, noting H1 2026 revenue of IDR 9.5 trillion (+6.8%) and net profit of IDR 1.9 trillion, and recommends a buy on weakness with a target price of IDR 3,800‑4,000 per share despite JSMR’s IDR 100 trillion liabilities.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) announces Rp 6.54 trillion shareholder loan to PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC)
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) disclosed an internal affiliate transaction in which its subsidiary PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) extended a shareholder loan of Rp 6.54 trillion to PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC). The loan reduces JSMR’s cash balance from Rp 7.08 trillion (June 2026) and increases other receivables by the same amount, with no immediate effect on consolidated revenue or expenses. For the first half of 2026, JSMR reported toll revenue of Rp 9.50 trillion (up 6.8%) and net profit of Rp 1.91 trillion (up 2.01%), while total liabilities stood at Rp 99.98 trillion. Mirae Asset Sekuritas recommends PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) with a target price of Rp 3,240 per share, noting that the loan is a neutral short‑term liquidity move and that future stock performance will depend on traffic growth, tariff adjustments, and new projects.

results.title: SSIA Maintains Rp400 Billion Profit Target; JSMR and BMAS Plan Corporate Actions
results.body: SSIA reaffirmed its 2026 net profit target of Rp400 billion while revising its revenue outlook to Rp7.20 trillion and allocating Rp2.20 trillion in capex, primarily for land acquisition and a Bali resort rebranding. JSMR disclosed a 2026 capex budget of Rp12 trillion, with Rp4.40 trillion already spent, and projected that about 62 km of toll roads, including sections of the Jogja‑Bawen and Patimban Access projects, will be operational by the end of 2026 or early 2027. BMAS announced a rights issue (PMHMETD IV) at Rp350 per share, aiming to raise roughly Rp1.01 trillion, representing 13.70 % of its capital, with the offering scheduled for 27 Nov‑3 Dec 2026 and Kasikorn Vision Financial Company Pte Ltd intending to exercise all its rights. The corporate actions are presented amid a broader market backdrop of a 0.12 % decline in the IHSG and foreign net selling of Rp621.40 billion.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk reports net profit of Rp1.91 trillion for H1 2026 and outlines five new toll projects
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk reported operating revenue of Rp10.31 trillion in the first half of 2026, with net profit attributable to the parent reaching Rp1.91 trillion, up 2.0% YoY. Revenue grew 7.6% YoY, driven by toll revenue of Rp9.5 trillion (up 6.8%) and other business revenue of Rp798.2 billion (up 17.6%); EBITDA rose 8.1% to Rp6.99 trillion, maintaining a margin of 67.8%. The company now manages 36 concessions covering 1,736 km, operating about 1,294 km, roughly 42% of Indonesia’s toll network. It also announced progress on five new toll projects, including Jakarta‑Cikampek Selatan II (Setu to Sadang), a 14‑km Patimban access road slated for 2028, and the Jogja‑Bawen corridor with section 1 targeting SLO by end‑September 2026 and section 6 already test‑operational this year.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk Plans Rp 12 Trillion Capex for 2026 and Explores New Toll Road Investments
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk is exploring potential investments in new toll roads and has allocated a capital expenditure budget of Rp 12 trillion for 2026. As of the first half of 2026, the company has realized Rp 4.4 trillion in capex for operations, maintenance, and toll road construction. The state-owned enterprise is open to both greenfield and brownfield toll projects, with investment decisions based on traffic prospects, connectivity, feasibility, and financial capacity. Additionally, Jasa Marga is participating in a streamlining initiative led by the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises and the Danantara sovereign wealth fund to optimize its portfolio.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk Absorbs Rp4.4 Trillion Capex, Highlights Toll Road Project Progress
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk reported that it absorbed Rp4.4 trillion in capital expenditure during the first semester of 2026, a portion of its Rp12 trillion capex allocation for the year, to finance operations, maintenance, and five ongoing toll road projects. The company also posted a net profit of Rp1.91 trillion, revenue of Rp10.31 trillion, and EBITDA of Rp6.99 trillion, with a 67.8% margin, while maintaining a gearing ratio of 1.2 and an interest coverage ratio of 3.9. Progress updates include provisional handovers and commercial operations on several segments of the Jakarta-Cikampek II Selatan, Akses Patimban, Jogja-Bawen, Jogja-Solo, and Probolinggo-Banyuwangi toll roads. PT Jasa Marga Tbk manages 36 concessions covering 1,736 km, with 1,294 km already operating, representing about 42% of Indonesia’s toll network.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk Announces Rp1.1 Trillion Dividend for FY 2025, Reaffirms Stable Payout Policy
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk announced a dividend of Rp1.1 trillion, representing 31 % of its FY 2025 net profit, underscoring its commitment to a stable dividend payout ratio. The payout was approved by the Rapat Umum Pemegang Saham and explained by President Director Rivan A. Purwantono at Public Expose Live 2026. For the first half of 2026, the company posted 7.6 % year‑on‑year growth in non‑construction revenue, an 8.1 % rise in EBITDA to a 67.8 % margin, and maintained a gearing ratio of 1.23 × and interest coverage ratio of 3.9 ×, both comfortably within covenant limits. Leveraging its long‑term toll concession and defensive business model, PT Jasa Marga Tbk aims to balance sustainable value creation, internal capital expansion, and shareholder returns.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk shifts investment focus to existing toll roads amid limited new tenders
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk said it will prioritize brownfield investments in its operating toll roads as new road tenders remain scarce, with projects slated for operation by late 2026‑early 2027. The company forecast capex of about Rp12 trillion for the year, reported H1 net profit of Rp1.91 trillion (up 2% YoY) and a 7.6% rise in non‑construction revenue to Rp10.31 trillion, while capex absorption reached Rp4.4 trillion in the first half.

results.title: Economist: Whoosh takeover will reshape Indonesia’s fiscal position
results.body: Kementerian Keuangan plans to take over management of the Jakarta‑Bandung high‑speed rail (Whoosh) on 15 September 2026, using a Special Mission Vehicle that can generate Rp3‑4 trillion of profit annually plus an estimated Rp800 billion from Whoosh operations, while the project’s US$7.2 billion debt to China Development Bank and daily ridership of about 17 000 passengers remain unchanged. Economist Yusuf Rendy Manilet says the shift will move fiscal pressure onto state‑owned enterprises KAI, WIKA, Jasa Marga and PSBI (which posted a Rp5 trillion loss in H1), with the government potentially holding 60 % of the SMV and China retaining 40 %.

results.title: Indonesia Finance Minister Purbaya Plans to Settle Whoosh High-Speed Rail Debt via Special Mission Vehicle Under Ministry of Finance
results.body: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa outlined a plan to resolve the Jakarta-Bandung high-speed rail (Whoosh) debt through a Special Mission Vehicle (SMV) under the Ministry of Finance, which would assume the project's liabilities. Danantara will transfer Whoosh to the Ministry via an inbreng scheme where the Ministry takes a 60% stake in PT Pilar Sinergi BUMN Indonesia, the majority shareholder of operator PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China, at zero cost to the state. The designated SMV, which currently generates Rp3–4 trillion in annual profit, is projected to add Rp800 billion from managing Whoosh, which Purbaya says is sufficient to service the approximately Rp79 trillion debt carrying a 3.4% interest rate. The project, developed by a consortium of state-owned enterprises PT KAI, PT Wijaya Karya Tbk, and PT Jasa Marga Tbk, has accumulated US$7.2 billion in investment including a US$1.2 billion cost overrun, financed 75% by China Development Bank loans and 25% equity from PT Pilar Sinergi BUMN Indonesia (60%) and Beijing Yawan HSR (40%). The government previously injected Rp3.2 trillion in state capital (PMN) into KAI while CDB provided an additional US$448 million loan, with studies estimating a 38-year investment recovery period.

results.title: M+G Investment Funds (7) - M+G Global Emerging Markets Fund Buy Shares of Jasa Marga
results.body: M+G Investment Funds (7) - M+G Global Emerging Markets Fund purchased 3,258,700 Jasa Marga shares at an average price of IDR 2,924 per share, costing IDR 9,522,965,100. The buy raised its stake from 4.990% to 5.040%, increasing its holding to 365,685,500 shares.

results.title: Analysts Recommend Buying Jasa Marga with Target Price of Rp 3,850
results.body: The article presents analyst recommendations for PT Jasa Marga Tbk, highlighting its solid profitability in the first half of 2026. Jasa Marga reported semester‑I 2026 revenue of Rp 13.11 trillion, a 6 % YoY decline, while toll revenue rose 6.8 % to Rp 9.5 trillion and construction revenue fell 35.8 % to Rp 2.8 trillion. EBITDA reached Rp 7.0 trillion, up 8.1 % YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 67.8 % and net profit of Rp 1.91 trillion, up 2.01 % YoY, driving gross margin to 46.6 % and net margin to 14.6 %. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia analyst Sukarno Alatas recommends a buy rating with a target price of Rp 3,850, while Infovesta Kapital Advisori analyst Ester Mulyani suggests buying on a breakout above Rp 3,000 with a near‑term target of Rp 3,100‑3,200. The analysts cite continued toll traffic, tariff adjustments and potential asset‑recycling initiatives with Danantara as growth catalysts, while noting high leverage and financing costs as key risks.

results.title: Jasa Marga records 647.5 million vehicle transactions in H1 2026, revenue falls 6% YoY
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk reported handling 647.5 million vehicle transactions in the first half of 2026, a 1.7% increase year-over-year, with average daily traffic of 3.58 million vehicles. The company’s total revenue for the semester was Rp 13.11 trillion, down 6% YoY, of which toll revenue contributed Rp 9.5 trillion. EBITDA reached Rp 7.0 trillion, maintaining a margin of 67.8%, and net profit attributable to shareholders rose 2.01% YoY to Rp 1.91 trillion. Jasa Marga operated 1,294 km of toll roads (42% of Indonesia’s network) and is advancing projects such as the Jakarta-Cikampek II Selatan and Patimban access tolls to strengthen connectivity.

results.title: Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia forecasts IHSG 6,300-6,650 in September, recommends nine stocks with up to 76% upside
results.body: Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia projects the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) to trade between 6,300 and 6,650 in September 2026, with a 40-45% chance of closing in the green zone after the index closed at 6,599.94 on 1 September, up 1.14%. The broker recommends nine Indonesian stocks, citing target prices and upside potentials: PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (target Rp4,800, upside 76%), PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (target Rp6,300, upside 43%), PT Pantai Indah Kapuk Dua Tbk (target Rp9,925, upside 65%), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (target Rp3,600, upside 29%), PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk (target Rp705, upside 44%), PT Jasa Marga Tbk (target Rp3,850, upside 41%), PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (target Rp3,140, upside 60%), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (target Rp970, upside 24%), and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (target Rp4,100, upside 26%). Kiwoom notes that the recommendations reflect strong commodity fundamentals, corporate buybacks, infrastructure projects and merger synergies supporting earnings growth. The report also highlights upcoming market changes, including a minimum stock price of Rp1, revised auto‑rejection thresholds (ARA/ARB), and the FTSE Russell rebalancing on 21 September, which could affect trading dynamics.

results.title: Phintraco Sekuritas forecasts IHSG consolidation ahead of key data releases and recommends six stocks, including JSMR
results.body: Phintraco Sekuritas expects the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) to trade within a 6,450‑6,570 range on Tuesday as investors await upcoming domestic and international data releases. The broker notes the index closed at 6,525.48, up 0.11%, marking a 4.64% month‑on‑month gain in August despite a 24.53% year‑to‑date correction. In its research, Phintraco recommends six potential‑gain stocks, naming JSMR as one of the picks. The outlook is underpinned by expectations of a 0.2% month‑on‑month rise in Indonesia’s inflation to 3.13% year‑on‑year in August, a narrowed trade deficit to US$0.3 billion in July, and a slight increase in the Manufacturing PMI to 50.5.

results.title: PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China share transfer from BUMN consortium to Ministry of Finance slated for September, says Danantara
results.body: Danantara said the transfer of state‑owned enterprise (BUMN) shares in PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China to a Special Mission Vehicle of the Ministry of Finance is targeted for completion in September. Currently 60 % of PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China is owned by the consortium PT Pilar Sinergi BUMN Indonesia, whose members are PT Kereta Api Indonesia (Persero), PT Wijaya Karya (Persero) Tbk, PT Jasa Marga (Persero) Tbk and PT Perkebunan Nusantara (Persero); the remaining 40 % is held by the Chinese consortium Beijing Yawan HSR Co. Ltd. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa explained the shares will be managed by an SMV to avoid a direct APBN burden and stressed that the project’s estimated debt of Rp79 trillion will not be transferred to the state budget. The specific SMV has not yet been identified, and the transfer is being accelerated to meet the mid‑September deadline.

results.title: Jasa Marga launches Travoy digital platform to enhance toll‑road user experience
results.body: Jasa Marga Tbk launched Travoy, a digital ecosystem designed to enhance toll‑road user experience. Travoy integrates travel‑planning information, RFID‑based touch‑less payments, digital receipts, a One Call Center 133 for roadside assistance, and a Travoy Rest feature that shows rest‑area facilities such as fuel stations and electric‑vehicle chargers. In the same announcement, the company reported Q1 2026 revenue of Rp5.1 trillion, up 10.4% year‑on‑year, with toll revenue of Rp4.7 trillion (+9.4%) and other services revenue of Rp397.6 billion (+24.4%), and a net profit of Rp774.7 billion. The launch reflects Jasa Marga’s broader digital transformation strategy amid rising electric‑vehicle adoption and changing mobility patterns.

results.title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk posts 6% revenue decline but 2% profit increase in H1 2026
results.body: PT Jasa Marga Tbk reported its first‑half 2026 results, with revenue falling 6% year‑on‑year to Rp 13.11 trillion while net profit attributable to the parent rose 2% YoY to Rp 1.91 trillion. Toll operations contributed Rp 9.5 trillion of revenue, construction Rp 2.8 trillion and other activities Rp 798.23 billion, and cost of revenue decreased to Rp 7 trillion. Gross profit increased 8.41% YoY to Rp 6.1 trillion and basic earnings per share rose to Rp 263. The company’s total assets grew to Rp 163.21 trillion, liabilities to Rp 99.98 trillion, equity to Rp 63.23 trillion, and cash and cash equivalents to Rp 7.08 trillion as of 30 June 2026.

results.title: Jasa Marga reports first-half 2026 profit of Rp1.9 trillion
results.body: PT Jasa Marga (Persero) Tbk reported a net profit of Rp1.9 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 2 % increase year‑on‑year. Revenue rose 7.6 % to Rp10.3 trillion, driven by toll revenue of Rp9.5 trillion (up 6.8 %) and other business revenue of Rp798.2 billion (up 17.6 %). EBITDA reached Rp7 trillion, an 8.1 % rise, maintaining an EBITDA margin of 67.8 %. The company recorded 647.5 million vehicle trips, a 1.7 % increase, and operated 1,294 km of its 1,736 km concession network while advancing several new toll projects.
